records.citation: Alabama State Bar Rules for Mandatory Continuing Legal Education, Rule 3 (CLE Requirement), Rule 7 (Annual Reporting), and Rule 9 (Professionalism)
records.governing_body: Alabama State Bar MCLE Commission (Alabama Supreme Court-authorized)
records.cycle_type: calendar-year fixed
records.cycle_description: Rule 3.A requires every attorney subject to the rules to complete a minimum of 12 hours of approved MCLE annually, 1 hour of which must be ethics or professionalism (the ethics hour counts toward, not in addition to, the 12). Compliance year is the calendar year (Jan 1-Dec 31). Rule 7.B requires each attorney to certify their annual report of compliance to the MCLE Commission by February 15 of the following year (Rule 7.A/7.B). Rule 8 deems an attorney who fails to earn 12 hours by Dec 31 non-compliant, requiring a deficiency plan by March 1 and completion by March 15, with escalating late fees (Reg. 8.2-8.5). Rule 9 separately requires new admittees to complete a 3-hour professionalism course within 12 months of admission. Up to 12 hours (including 1 ethics hour) may be carried forward one year (Rule 6.B).

records.sourcing_notes: Both the Alabama State Bar's own plain-English FAQ page and the full MCLE Rule Book PDF (Revised August 2025) were fetched and read directly, including the complete text of Rules 1-9; the two sources agree in full on the 12-hour/1-ethics-hour requirement and the Feb 15 reporting deadline.

records.citation: Alaska Bar Rule 65 (Continuing Legal Education) and Bar Rule 66 (Noncompliance with CLE Requirements; Suspension)
records.governing_body: Alaska Bar Association (per Alaska Supreme Court Order)
records.cycle_type: calendar-year fixed
records.cycle_description: Bar Rule 65(a) requires every active member to complete at least 12 CLE credit hours per calendar year, 3 of which must be approved ethics CLE (MECLE) covering topics such as professional responsibility, workplace ethics, malpractice prevention, or wellness. This 12-hour figure (increased from a prior lower requirement) took effect under SCO 2016/SCO 2044, effective January 1, 2025, with the first reporting deadline under the new rule falling February 1, 2026. Rule 65(b) allows carryforward of up to 12 credits earned in the immediately preceding calendar year. Rule 65(c) requires each member to certify by February 1 of each year whether the 3 MECLE hours and 9 other CLE hours were completed in the preceding year (or carried over). Rule 66 provides for a notice of noncompliance and, absent cure within 30 days, suspension. New admittees are exempt for their calendar year of admission (Rule 65(g)(2)).
records.next_deadline_computed_note: Sourcing groundwork only; annual certification deadline is Feb 1 per Rule 65(c) - actual next-deadline computation not performed in this pass.

records.citation: C.R.C.P. Rule 250.2 (CLE Requirements) and Rule 250.7 (Compliance)
records.governing_body: Colorado Supreme Court Office of Attorney Regulation Counsel / Continuing Legal and Judicial Education (CLJE) Committee
records.cycle_type: 36-month (3-year) rolling compliance period keyed to each attorney's individual admission date - a distinct shape from calendar-year, birth-month-rolling, or last-name-cohort systems
records.cycle_description: C.R.C.P. 250.2(1) requires every registered lawyer (and judge) to complete 45 CLE credit hours per compliance period, at least 7 of which must be professional responsibility hours - specifically (effective Jan 1, 2023) at least 2 hours in equity, diversity, and inclusivity plus at least 5 hours in legal ethics or legal professionalism. Rule 250.2(3): the FIRST compliance period begins on the attorney's individual date of admission and ends December 31 of the third full calendar year following admission (e.g., admitted May 10, 2019 -> first period ends Dec 31, 2022); each SUBSEQUENT compliance period is then a clean Jan 1-Dec 31 block spanning three full calendar years. Rule 250.7(2) requires each lawyer to verify their CLE transcript is accurate/complete no later than January 31 following the end of the compliance period. Rule 250.7(3): if hours are short, a make-up plan must be filed by Jan 31 and completed by May 31, reported by June 14. Colorado is self-reporting via online CLE transcript/affidavit. Licensed Legal Paraprofessionals (LLPs) have a separate, lower 30-hour/5-ethics-hour requirement under the same rule. No roll-over of excess credits into the next compliance period is permitted (250.2(8)); attorneys are exempt starting their 72nd birthday (250.2(9)(b)).
records.next_deadline_computed_note: Sourcing groundwork only; verification deadline is Jan 31 following the end of each individual 3-year compliance period, which itself is keyed to the attorney's admission date, not a fixed calendar trigger - actual next-deadline computation not performed in this pass and will require each attorney's admission date as an input.
records.sourcing_notes: Both the Colorado attorney regulation office's own plain-English CLE overview page (coloradolegalregulation.com/AboutUs/CLE.asp, reached via a 301 redirect from the older coloradosupremecourt.com domain) and the full official C.R.C.P. Rule 250 PDF (250.1 through 250.10, current through Rule Changes 2023(09)) were fetched and read directly; they agree. FLAGGING A NEW CYCLE SHAPE: Colorado's compliance period is neither a simple calendar-year system, nor a birth-month rolling 12-month period, nor a California-style fixed last-name cohort group - it is a 3-year period whose START is individually pegged to each attorney's admission date (with the FIRST period end year varying by admittee), after which periods synchronize to clean Jan-Dec 3-year blocks. This should probably be modeled as its own distinct cycle_type in the product schema rather than force-fit into the three shapes already in the dataset.

records.citation: Connecticut Practice Book Section 2-27A (Minimum Continuing Legal Education)
records.governing_body: Connecticut Judicial Branch / Minimum Continuing Legal Education Commission
records.cycle_type: calendar-year fixed
records.cycle_description: Per the Connecticut Judicial Branch's own MCLE page and MCLE FAQ page (both fetched and read directly, and in full agreement): attorneys must complete 12 credit hours of continuing legal education each calendar year, at least 2 of which must be in ethics and/or professionalism. Connecticut uses attorney self-certification rather than a proof-submission/audit system: no documentation is filed with the state, but attorneys must retain personal CLE records for 7 years, and must certify compliance (or an applicable exemption) on their annual attorney registration form the following year (e.g., 2017 CLE hours are certified when registering in 2018). Up to 2 excess credit hours may be carried forward to the following year. New admittees are not subject to the requirement until the calendar year following their admission to the Connecticut bar. The governing provision is Practice Book Section 2-27A(a)-(e), with related registration requirements in Section 2-27(d).

records.citation: Delaware Rules for Continuing Legal Education, Rule 4 (Educational Requirements) and Rule 5 (Compliance), promulgated by the Supreme Court of the State of Delaware
records.governing_body: Delaware Commission on Continuing Legal Education (Supreme Court of Delaware)
records.cycle_type: 24-month cohort by admission-year parity (even/odd admission year) -- new shape, not birth-month rolling, not last-name cohort
records.cycle_description: Rule 4(A): every attorney must complete a minimum of 24 approved CLE credit hours during each two-year period, at least 12 of which must be earned in-person/live, and at least 4 of the 24 hours must be approved Ethics credits. Up to 20 excess hours may carry forward (Ethics hours may only carry forward as general credit). Rule 5(A): the two-year Compliance Year cohort is fixed by the parity of the attorney's year of admission to the Delaware Bar -- attorneys admitted in even-numbered years must complete their credits by December 31 of every even-numbered year; attorneys admitted in odd-numbered years must complete by December 31 of every odd-numbered year. Senior Attorneys (40+ years admitted in any US jurisdiction) have a reduced requirement under Rule 4(C): 12 hours/2 years including 2 Ethics hours. Newly admitted attorneys additionally must complete 7 'Fundamentals' courses under Rule 4(D).

records.citation: Rule 6-10.3, Rules Regulating The Florida Bar (Minimum Continuing Legal Education Standards)
records.governing_body: The Florida Bar Board of Legal Specialization and Education, under the Supreme Court of Florida
records.cycle_type: 36-month (3-year) reporting cycle, individually assigned per member by The Florida Bar
records.cycle_description: Rule 6-10.3(b): every member must complete a minimum of 30 credit hours of approved CLE every 3 years. At least 3 of the 30 hours must be in approved technology courses. At least 5 of the 30 hours must be in approved legal ethics, professionalism, substance use disorder, or mental health and wellness courses; as part of those 5 hours each member must complete, every reporting cycle, the 2-credit-hour Florida Legal Professionalism course. Excess credits do not carry over (Rule 6-10.3(b), last sentence). Rule 6-10.4(b): each member must report by the last day of the member's 'applicable reporting period as assigned by The Florida Bar' -- the rule text does not specify the exact basis (e.g., admission date) on which individual reporting periods are assigned.

records.citation: Rules and Regulations for the Organization and Government of the State Bar of Georgia, Part VIII, Chapter 1, Rule 8-104 (Education Requirements and Exemptions), as amended by Georgia Supreme Court Order, In re: Motion to Amend 2024-2 (Case No. S25U0126, Nov. 10, 2025)
records.governing_body: Commission on Continuing Lawyer Competency (CCLC), State Bar of Georgia, under the Supreme Court of Georgia
records.cycle_type: 24-month (biennial) fixed calendar-period cycle -- same deadline for all members (not birth-month rolling, not a last-name cohort)
records.cycle_description: Rule 8-104(a): each active member must complete a minimum of 18 hours of CLE during each biennial compliance period, with up to 18 unused hours carryable to the immediately succeeding period only. Rule 8-104(b)(1)-(2): of those 18 hours, a minimum of 3 hours must be in legal ethics and a minimum of 2 hours must be in professionalism (each carryable up to the stated cap, one period only). Rule 8-102(c): the Biennial Compliance Period deadline of December 31 in every odd year is the SAME for all active, non-exempt members; the first biennial period runs January 1, 2026 - December 31, 2027. These rules, effective December 4, 2025 for the first Jan 1, 2026 compliance period, replaced Georgia's prior annual 12-hour/1-ethics/1-professionalism structure and eliminated the trial-hours requirement for trial lawyers.

records.citation: Idaho Bar Commission Rules (I.B.C.R.), Section IV, Rule 402 (Education Requirement - Report)
records.governing_body: Idaho State Bar, Board of Commissioners, under the Supreme Court of the State of Idaho
records.cycle_type: 36-month (3-year) reporting period, individually assigned per attorney based on the attorney's own admission date (or transfer-to-active/reinstatement date) -- not a birth-month rolling cycle and not a shared last-name or admission-year cohort
records.cycle_description: Rule 402(a)(1): Active and House Counsel Members must complete a minimum of thirty (30) credit hours of Accredited Activity in every three (3) year reporting period. Rule 402(a)(2): at least three (3) of those CLE credits must be in courses on legal ethics or professional responsibility. Rule 402(b)(2)(A): for a newly admitted attorney, the individual reporting period begins on the date of admission to the Bar and ends December 31 of the third full calendar year following admission (an analogous rule keys the period to the effective date of transfer to Active status, or to the pre-cancellation reporting period on reinstatement). Newly admitted attorneys with under 3 years of prior practice also must complete a New Attorney Program with 10 NAC-Approved credits addressing Idaho practice/procedure/ethics (Rule 402(f)).

records.citation: Indiana Rules for Admission to the Bar and the Discipline of Attorneys, Rule 29 (Mandatory Continuing Legal Education)
records.governing_body: Indiana Commission for Continuing Legal Education / Indiana Supreme Court Office of Admissions & Continuing Education
records.cycle_type: 3-year rolling 'Educational Period' (individualized per attorney, sequential once each 3-year period ends) with an annual 6-hour floor
records.cycle_description: Ind. Admis. & Disc. R. 29 requires every attorney to complete no less than 6 hours of Approved Courses each year, AND no less than 36 hours of Approved Courses during each 3-year 'Educational Period' (defined as 'a three-year period during which an Attorney must complete thirty-six (36) hours of Approved Courses'; periods 'shall be sequential, in that once an Attorney's particular three-year period terminates, a new three-year period and thirty-six hour minimum shall commence').
